data.description:
## Observation
In an isolated scratch store (2026-11-18 PST), `rebar.llm.verify_completion("cushiony-feathered-anura", source="local")` failed at the provider (403, dummy AWS credentials). The failure path wrote a `COMPLETION_VERDICT` event with `schema: gate_error_v1` into a NEW directory `.tickets-tracker/cushiony-feathered-anura/` instead of the ticket's canonical directory `7689-bdbe-e709-49ef/`, and committed it. Every later `verify_completion` call by alias then failed with `rebar show failed (exit 1): ticket "cushiony-feathered-anura" has no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event`, because the alias now resolved to the stray directory.

`emit_gate_error` (src/rebar/llm/gate_error_sidecar.py) passes the caller's `ticket_id` straight to `append_event` without resolving it to the canonical id. Callers: src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py (5 sites) and src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py.

`origin/tickets` currently has no alias-named directories (checked 2026-11-18), so the production MCP path has not hit this yet; the path that has is a library call with an alias.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A regression test calls a failing gate run with an alias and asserts the gate_error sidecar lands in the canonical ticket directory and no alias-named directory is created.
- [ ] The gate_error sidecar emitter resolves the ticket id to its canonical directory before appending.
data.title: A failed gate run called with an alias writes its gate_error sidecar into a new alias-named ticket directory
